sources.title: Introducing GPT-5.2
sources.evidence: Original December 11, 2025 announcement makes the models available that day and explicitly maps GPT-5.2 Instant to gpt-5.2-chat-latest, separately from Thinking and Pro. The Instant API release is explicit; the xhigh reasoning controls described there apply to Thinking and Pro. Reopened for the October 27 parameter re-audit: no nominal size or size-bearing named base is specified for Instant.

sources.title: GPT-5.2 Chat API documentation
sources.evidence: Exact alias documentation lists text/image input, text output, 128,000 context, 16,384 maximum output, Chat Completions/Responses and function calling. It also lists a contradictory 272,000 maximum input. It marks the model shut down and lists only the undated alias; no reasoning or prompt-caching feature flag is present. Fresh full Markdown read for the parameter re-audit contains no total or active parameter specification.

sources.title: Update to GPT-5 System Card: GPT-5.2
sources.evidence: Reopened the original December 11, 2025 PDF for the October 27 parameter re-audit and searched its complete freshly fetched text. Sections 1-2 distinguish Instant from Thinking and describe data and reinforcement learning; exact Instant safety, vision and health columns report evaluation scores. No nominal total/active count or size-bearing named base is given. Generic reasoning-training prose is not treated as proof about Instant.

sources.title: GPT-5.5 Instant System Card
sources.evidence: Reopened the May 4, 2026 original PDF and searched its complete freshly fetched text for the parameter re-audit. Exact gpt-5.2-instant columns in safety, vision and health comparisons report scores, not total/active counts. The card warns that previous-model values can reflect later versions. GPT-5.5-specific details are not transferred to GPT-5.2 Instant.

sources.title: Investigating the consequences of accidentally grading CoT during RL
sources.evidence: Reopened the May 7, 2026 OpenAI training article. It explicitly identifies GPT-5.2 Instant among released models affected by inadvertent CoT grading during reinforcement learning and qualifies GPT-5 Instant CoT as limited. It gives no nominal parameter count, expert layout or named base with a disclosed size; the later GPT-5.4 Instant ablations do not establish GPT-5.2 Instant size.

sources.title: Prompt caching
sources.evidence: Current guide explains caching and lists gpt-5.2 among models supporting extended retention, but does not name gpt-5.2-chat-latest in that list. Support for the distinct Thinking alias is not transferred to this Chat alias as structural evidence.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: Archived guide explicitly covers models before GPT-5.6 and explains caching through Transformer attention key/value tensors. Its model table names gpt-5.2, not the Chat alias. Together with cached-input pricing alone, it does not establish exact Instant structure under this audit evidence standard.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Directly read guide: Responses handles PDFs by extracting text and page images for vision-capable models; Chat Completions also accepts PDF file content. Applied to this exact model’s documented vision and endpoint support, this establishes PDF as an API input format, not a separate native sensory modality.

sources.title: API deprecations
sources.evidence: May 8, 2026 notice names gpt-5.2-chat-latest and gives August 10, 2026 as its shutdown date. The exact current model page independently marks it shut down. Documentation was checked; no authenticated endpoint operation was tested.

sources.title: API changelog
sources.evidence: February 10, 2026 entry explicitly updates gpt-5.2-chat-latest to the latest model used in ChatGPT. Confirms a mutable alias rather than an immutable December checkpoint; no dated OpenAI snapshot is supplied by the current exact model page.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Current agreement grants limited hosted-service use and reserves service intellectual property in section 9.1. Supports a descriptive proprietary classification, not a downloadable-weight license or an assertion that current contract wording applied on launch day.

sources.title: All OpenAI API models
sources.evidence: Current model catalog lists GPT-5.2 Chat as shut down and separately identifies its Apache-2.0 open-weight gpt-oss releases. GPT-5.2 Chat is documented as a hosted model, with no released weight distribution in the reviewed publisher materials.

sources.title: Azure models sold directly by Azure
sources.evidence: Exact gpt-5.2-chat rows for 2025-12-11 and 2026-02-10 independently specify a 128,000 context, 111,616 input and 16,384 output, plus tool/function calling. These corroborate historical context, but Azure-specific version labels and retirement dates are not assigned to OpenAI’s endpoint.

sources.title: GPT-5.3 Instant System Card
sources.evidence: Freshly opened the March 3, 2026 original five-page PDF and read its complete cached text. Tables 1-3 explicitly include gpt-5.2-instant in safety, mental-health and HealthBench comparisons; they contain no parameter column. The successor introduction describes capabilities and a shared safety-mitigation approach, not an unchanged named base with a disclosed size. No total or active parameter count appears in the document.

sources.title: Step 3.5 Flash: Open Frontier-Level Intelligence with 11B Active Parameters
sources.evidence: Freshly opened the original model-team report and its post-training comparison Table 5. Separate Activated params and Total params rows both show a dash for GPT-5.2 xHigh. This is a Thinking comparison, not the GPT-5.2 Instant/chat-latest target, so it supplies neither a count nor an exact-variant disclosure. It is retained as the inspected later active-count comparison lead, not OpenAI size evidence.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 re-audit reopened the launch, exact Chat documentation, original card, later GPT-5.3/GPT-5.5 Instant comparisons and OpenAI training research. None reports a nominal total or an explicit relationship to a named base with a disclosed size. Bounded fresh searches found no later first-party disclosure. StepFun Table 5 leaves GPT-5.2 xHigh total blank and refers to Thinking, not this Instant alias.

active_parameters_b.note: Rechecked active count independently: the exact Instant sources disclose no activated-parameter count. The later StepFun model-team Table 5 has an explicit Activated params row, but its GPT-5.2 xHigh cell is blank and identifies a different variant. Fresh exact-alias/Instant searches found no original model-team active-count comparison for this target; no dense-equals-active or sibling-count inference is made.

architecture.note: Targeted first-party training and interpretability searches did not yield an exact structural disclosure. Exact Chat docs show cached-input pricing but no caching feature binding; the pre-5.6 KV-cache mechanism alone is insufficient to assign Transformer to this variant. No dense/MoE inference.

context_window.note: The exact OpenAI HTML and Markdown model pages specify 128,000 context; Azure exact-version rows corroborate it. OpenAI Markdown also says 272,000 maximum input, an unresolved contradiction; this is not used to inflate the explicitly named context. Output limit is 16,384.

modalities.note: Native model modalities are text/image input and text output. PDF is included as the API file format processed into text and page images, justified by exact vision and Responses/Chat Completions support; no native audio/video claim.

reasoning.note: Launch binds this alias to GPT-5.2 Instant; later OpenAI RL research explicitly reports CoT grading for that exact variant and qualifies Instant CoT as limited. This supports reasoning capability, not user-configurable effort levels, adaptive reasoning, or routing to the separate Thinking model.

tool_call.note: Exact model documentation explicitly supports function calling; Azure’s exact variant rows independently corroborate it. This describes last-documented capability, not current endpoint availability.

patch.notes: The original 2025-12-11 launch maps gpt-5.2-chat-latest to GPT-5.2 Instant, separately from Thinking and Pro. This was a mutable alias, explicitly updated on 2026-02-10; the current OpenAI model page lists no dated immutable snapshot. Exact OpenAI documentation specifies 128,000 context and 16,384 maximum output, but its Markdown also gives an inconsistent 272,000 maximum input; Azure exact-version rows corroborate 128,000 context. OpenAI training research explicitly establishes limited CoT for GPT-5.2 Instant; reasoning=true does not imply documented effort controls, adaptive reasoning or the ChatGPT router. PDF denotes API conversion to extracted text and page images. Total and active parameter counts are undisclosed for this Instant alias; no disclosed-size base lineage or exact active-count comparison supports a nominal inference. Architecture remains unverified. OpenAI’s deprecation notice gives 2026-08-10 as this alias’s shutdown date, consistent with its current model page. Specifications are historical documentation, not a successful endpoint test.

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter re-audit retains undisclosed total and active counts after reopening the original launch/card and exact documentation, OpenAI training research, and later GPT-5.3/GPT-5.5 Instant comparisons. A newly checked StepFun activated/total comparison leaves GPT-5.2 xHigh blank and concerns Thinking rather than Instant. No supported nominal count or disclosed-size base lineage was found. The other 12 assessments, including limited CoT, 128K context, alias mutability, documentation conflict and historical shutdown, are preserved.
